introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Computer Science 2 (0595), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2021. Duration: Two hours.**

Answer any FIVE questions. All questions carry 20 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are NOT allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) State the main technological feature that distinguished each of the following computer classifications:

- 1st generation
- 2nd generation
- 3rd generation
- 4th generation

(4 marks)

(ii) In computer programming:

- What are mnemonics? (2 marks)
- State two disadvantages of using machine code. (2 marks)
- State two differences between a compiler and an interpreter. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Generations of computers (4 marks, 1 mark each)**

| Generation | Main technological feature |
|---|---|
| 1st | Vacuum tubes (thermionic valves) |
| 2nd | Transistors |
| 3rd | Integrated circuits (ICs, several transistors on a silicon chip) |
| 4th | Microprocessors (a whole CPU on one chip, large-scale and very-large-scale integration) |

**(ii) Programming**

- **Mnemonics (2 marks).** Mnemonics are short, easy-to-remember abbreviations (symbolic codes) such as ADD, SUB, LDA or MOV that stand for machine instructions in an assembly language, so that the programmer does not have to write binary codes.
- **Two disadvantages of machine code (2 marks, 1 mark each).** Any two of: it is written in binary, so it is very difficult to read, write and learn; it is easy to make errors and hard to find and correct them (debugging); it takes a long time to write; it depends on the type of processor, so a program cannot be moved to a different type of computer.
- **Two differences between a compiler and an interpreter (2 marks, 1 mark each).** Any two of: a compiler translates the **whole** program into machine code **before** it is run, whereas an interpreter translates and executes it **one statement at a time**; a compiler produces an object (executable) file that can be run again without the source program, whereas an interpreter must translate the program again at every run; a compiler reports all the errors after the translation, whereas an interpreter stops at the first error it meets; compiled programs run faster.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) One of the health hazards of using computers is RSI.

(i) Write RSI in full. (1 mark)

(ii) State two body parts that are likely to be affected by RSI. (2 marks)

(iii) What should we do in order to prevent RSI? (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) RSI (1 mark).** RSI stands for **Repetitive Strain Injury**.

**(ii) Two body parts (2 marks, 1 mark each).** Any two of: the wrists, the fingers or hands, the forearms, the elbows, the neck, the shoulders or the back.

**(iii) Prevention (1 mark).** Take regular short breaks and do stretching exercises; sit with a good posture, with the keyboard and mouse at a comfortable height (use an ergonomic keyboard or a wrist rest); avoid typing or clicking for long periods without a break.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) State two advantages and two disadvantages of using electronic mail as a means of communication. (4 marks)

(ii) State a difference between intranet and extranet. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Electronic mail (4 marks, 1 mark each)**

- *Advantages (any two):* messages are delivered almost instantly, anywhere in the world; it is cheap compared with post or telephone; files such as documents and pictures can be attached; the same message can be sent to many people at once; it can be read from any device connected to the Internet, at any time; a copy of the message is kept.
- *Disadvantages (any two):* it needs a computer (or phone) and an Internet connection; spam (unwanted mail) and attachments can carry viruses; messages can be misread because there is no tone of voice or face-to-face contact; the sender cannot be sure that the receiver has read the message; there is a risk of fraud (phishing) and of loss of privacy.

**(ii) Intranet and extranet (2 marks).** An **intranet** is a private network of an organisation (for example a school), built with Internet technology and open only to its own members or staff. An **extranet** is an intranet that is also opened, through the Internet and with a password, to selected outsiders such as customers, suppliers or partners; the intranet itself is not open to them.
